newsitem.title: FINLAND: January spending-spree keeps Helsinki peaking.
newsitem.headline: January spending-spree keeps Helsinki peaking.

text.p: Shares ended at a new all-time high on Tuesday but off intrasession peaks as a January buying spree continued after overnight gains on Wall Street.

The HEX index added over one percent to 2,543.68 in volume a solid 604 million markka, about one-quarter of it in Nokia which boosted the market right from the open, rising to match and surpass its New York close. It retreated slightly in late trade to end at 270.00 markka, up 4.50.
Kesko rose in heavy 85 million markka volume, ending up 1.50 markka at 65.90. It made up 13 percent of total turnover.
Brokers said the stock was boosted by weekend media reports suggesting the European Commission would give Kesko ample time to unwind its merger with Tuko, blocked by EU competition rules.
"An expected sharp rise in private consumption this year is also good news for Kesko and other retailers," one broker said.
Kemira reversed gains in lively trade, falling 0.90 markka to 57.60 after saying its pigments unit made an operating loss in 1996 -- it had warned earlier it would be near break-even.
But brokers were undaunted, saying they expected the stock to recover soon as the group result is likely to be positive.

Recently sluggish forestries firmed in broadly thin trade, as brokers said they tracked strength in U.S. and Swedish forestry issues. But UPM-Kymmene was active, ending up 0.70 markka at 98.50 after touching an intrasession high of 99.30.
